newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech end-Oct M2 up 11.4 pct yr/yr (+13.8 Sept).
newsitem.headline: Czech end-Oct M2 up 11.4 pct yr/yr (+13.8 Sept).

text.p: The key measure of Czech money supply, M2, was up 11.4 percent at the end of October, year-on-year, compared with 13.8 percent 12-month growth measured at the end of September, the Czech National Bank said on Tuesday.

Including the effect of a $1.32 billion equity expansion, money from which was deposited with the CNB in the third quarter of 1995, the end-October year-on-year increase was 9.8 percent, the CNB said.
The end-September figure -- including the SPT transaction -- was revised from the central bank's earlier report of 11.6 percent from the central bank's earlier report of 11.8 percent.
The end-September figure without the SPT factor was revised to 13.8 percent from 14.0 percent.
CZECH M2 MONEY OCT 1996 SEPT 1996 OCT 1995
Note. All 1996 figures subject to revision, figures reported previously by the CNB are in brackets.
Czech M2 measures currency, demand deposits, time and savings deposits, and foreign currency deposits.
The bottom figures exlude the effect of SPT Telecom's $1.32 billion equity expansion in the summer of 1995 which was put on deposit at the Czech National Bank (CNB).
The CNB said that the total of outstanding crown and foreign currency credits was up 10.7 percent, year-on-year, at the end of October from 12.1 percent at the end of September.
The volume of crown and foreign currency deposits was up 8.6 percent at the end of October compared with the end-September 12-month growth rate of 10.5 percent.
The average interest rate on credit granted by Czech banks in October was 13.78 percent, down from 13.96 percent in September, the CNB said.

The CNB, at the end of June, raised its key discount rate one full percentage point to 10.5 percent, and raised minimum reserve requirements for commercial banks to 11.5 percent from 8.5 percent, beginning on August 1.
